assessment.reasoning: Saanjh India is operating with compressed margins following a recent freight rate increase and during a quiet seasonal stretch without a festival anchor. A previous free-shipping trial was deemed successful on conversion alone without measuring contribution, masking true margin erosion. Testing any promotion now—such as free shipping (costing Rs.30/order) or flat/percent discounts—requires significant incremental conversion lifts just to break even on contribution (e.g., free shipping requires conversion to rise from 15.6% to 16.59%). Because 14% of customers are price-insensitive Bulk Regulars and 17% are Lapsing Loyalists who already know the catalog, sitewide or broad promotions heavily subsidize full-price baseline demand. Given that a single experiment costs roughly 2.8x the annual promotional profit pool and only 1 experiment slot remains, spending it during an off-peak period against aggressive competitor discounting (20% off sitewide) carries a negative expected value.

assessment.reasoning: Nutbox Labs faces operational and inventory bottlenecks rather than structural price resistance. The nearest competitor successfully passed an 8% price increase without losing market share, proving category demand is resilient to price. Meanwhile, conversion drift is tied to non-price issues: damaged packaging on heavier SKUs and stockouts of popular lines. Furthermore, 27% of customers are price-insensitive bulk buyers who order on fixed salary-week schedules; discounting them subsidizes purchases that would occur at full margin. With only 1 experiment available (costing 2.8x the annual promotional profit pool), running a discount campaign would dilute contribution margin without solving the root causes of conversion drift.
